gaps.sentence: The cafe ___ we first met has closed down.
gaps.hint: location: we met in the cafe
gaps.explanation: 'Where' replaces 'in which' for places; 'which' would need a preposition ('in which').

gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.

gaps.sentence: She was two hours late, ___ annoyed the interviewer.
gaps.hint: comment on the whole situation before the comma
gaps.explanation: When a clause comments on the whole previous statement, use 'which' after the comma.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: The winner, ___ was only seventeen, broke the championship record.
gaps.hint: person as subject after a comma
gaps.explanation: The clause adds extra information about a person, so 'who' is required and 'that' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: Show me ___ you have written so far.
gaps.explanation: 'What you have written' means 'the things that you have written'; 'that' cannot head a nominal clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: 1998 was the year ___ the factory finally closed.
The house ___ stands on the corner dates from 1870.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is needed because a house is a thing; 'where' would introduce information about location, not a subject.
